title: Priority-lane equalizer to resolve cross-tenant TTFT delta
creator: Lena Park
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported a sudden 2-4x increase in TTFT for short-turn interactive requests (1-5 token responses) starting 2026-03-11 07:00 UTC. Token/sec throughput for long sessions also shows increased variance. Preliminary correlation indicates the regression coincides with the kernel-selector rollout that added a latency-optimized microkernel for quantized variants.

Observed behavior: In production, a subset of requests (high-priority lanes and low concurrency short sessions) are getting deferred behind warmup-heavy fanouts. The scheduler is occasionally mis-weighing warmup cost vs. priority weight, causing high-priority tokens/sec to drop and first-token latency (TTFT) to spike. Effect is amplified on Dedicated pools with heterogeneous tenant model mixes and on Private clusters with uneven cold caches.

Root cause hypothesis: The kernel selector update introduced a heuristic that increases affinity to microkernels for quantized model families. When combined with the new warmup-cost estimator, the scheduler over-prefers grouping requests for kernel conversion, which creates transient warmup waves. High-priority lanes are starved during those waves because the priority scoring does not account for pending warmup delta.

Impact: Customer-facing TTFT regressions reported by 3 mid-market customers (support tickets #C-2145, #C-2161, #C-2172) and automated SLO alerting for hosted API. Dedicated customers see degraded p95 TTFT in region-us-west-2. Private deployments reported increased retry rates tied to client-side timeouts.

Immediate mitigation (already applied):
- Deployed a conservative scheduler patch to preferentially preempt warmup grouping for requests with explicit priority tags (applied 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC).
- Enabled a soft-fairness token dispenser that guarantees minimal dispatch slots for each priority lane per worker (temporary config flag).
- Rerouted a small percentage (5%) of traffic to verified legacy kernel path for affected quantized variants for canary validation (hosted only).

Planned permanent fix:
1) Implement "Priority-lane Equalizer" algorithm in scheduler: compute an exponential moving average of warmup cost per kernel variant and subtract a smoothed penalty from affinity scores to prevent repeated grouping bursts.
2) Extend KV-cache warmup metadata to include last-warmup-age so scheduler can prefer workers with warm caches for high-priority short sessions.
3) Add telemetry counters and a lightweight circuit-breaker that opens when high-priority lane TTFT diverges >30% vs baseline for >2m.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit + integration tests for scheduler heuristic (simulated shard, warmup, and priority mixes) in repo/tests/scheduler/priority_equalizer_test.go.
- Staging validation with traffic replay of last 72h customer traces.
- Canary rollout: Hosted 2% -> 10% -> 50% over 36 hours with automated health checks (ttft p50/p95, token/sec, error-rate).
- Dedicated rollout: opt-in by pool owners, starting with non-production pools, then production pools with a 2-hour observation window.
- Private: produce a patch build and runbook for on-prem customers; coordinate with SEs for upgrade windows.

Monitoring and KPIs:
- Dashboard: /dashboards/latency/priority-lane-equalizer (p50/p95 TTFT per-priority, tokens/sec by model family).
- Alerts: restore SLO if p95 TTFT regresses >15% for more than 10 minutes after rollout step.

Open trade-offs:
- Slightly less aggressive batching could increase per-token cost by ~3% in edge cases; but matching SLOs for high-priority short sessions is higher priority for enterprise customers.
- Full KV-cache metadata propagation adds ~1.2ms overhead per handshake; we will gate behind a rollout flag and measure.

Decision: Proceed with Priority-lane Equalizer as primary fix plus KV-cache last-warmup-age metadata as supportive optimization. Conservative scheduler patch remains as fallback.

Owner: Marco Diaz (runtime scheduler, lead). QA lead: Priya Desai. Customer communications: Sarah O'Neill (Solutions).
